source.title: Circuit Claims Depend on What Is Extracted and How It Is Compared

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses indirect-object identification as an example of extraction and reference choices, but its experiments use synthetic Lean tactic prediction, not GPT-2 IOI. It neither tests nor relies on the specified IOI circuit.
record.gate_note: The text mentions the IOI study and argues that changing the corrupted reference can change which heads appear necessary, but this is not a new IOI result. The paper's own synthetic-Lean circuit-extraction findings are recorded with versions ["none"]; cited IOI findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The experiments use synthetic Lean tactic-prediction transformers, not GPT-2 small or the IOI task. IOI appears only in the introduction, as an argued example: the corrupted reference is a design choice that may change which heads appear necessary. No IOI result is reported, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that preserving behaviour does not fix a circuit's interpretation; claims depend on the extracted graph, selection and tie-breaking, Q/K representation, loss budget and comparison level. They recommend reporting these choices together with random baselines and controls.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic Lean tactic-prediction models and compares learned-mask core/support graphs, loss-budget pruning graphs, and graph-comparison choices; it does not reproduce the GPT-2 small IOI circuit method.
record.method_sensitivity: Routing-head overlap falls sharply when selection among tied scores is randomized. The paper also varies graph object, query/key representation, pruning loss budget, and extraction repeat, and reports corresponding comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic-Lean checkpoints, dense-vs-sparse structural overlap is near a score-weighted random baseline. Routing-head overlap is high only under deterministic tie-breaking (0.666 vs 0.028 with random ties).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model circuit-overlap conclusions depend on the comparison unit and on how tied scores are broken.

fits_no_version.finding: Full bridge-node ablation in the 75%-sparse RL model reduces compositional exact match (to 0.295–0.940) while atomic exact match stays at 0.995–1.000. Effects differ at other checkpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In synthetic Lean tasks, compositional behaviour partly depends on core-circuit nodes outside the atomic-task circuits.

record.problems: The experiments use a controlled synthetic Lean benchmark and an 8-layer, approximately 415.7M-parameter model; generalization to other architectures and heterogeneous tasks is unvalidated. The authors note that the bridge-fraction association rests on only two curriculum conditions. Bridge-ablation effects vary across other checkpoints and tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI findings were reported. Other synthetic-Lean results, including extraction-order comparisons, bridge-fraction associations, boundary shifts, and supplementary controls, were not entered because they do not test the specified IOI behavior; only directly relevant general circuit-overlap and bridge-ablation outcomes are included.

untested.parts: All of it: GPT-2 small IOI, the 26 heads in 7 classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
All of it: no name-mover ablation and no backup or self-repair test.
All of it: no IOI circuit in other models, sizes or checkpoints, and no reuse of its components for other tasks.
All of it for IOI: method-sensitivity results are on synthetic-Lean models only.
All of it for IOI. The corrupted-reference argument is stated without an IOI experiment.
All of it: no IOI name orders, templates or number of names.

record.verdict_notes: IOI (Wang et al., 2023) is mentioned only as an illustrative argument in the introduction, with no experiment. The paper is methodologically relevant to V4 and V5 in spirit but tests neither on IOI.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small IOI behavior, 26 attention heads in 7 classes, their stated roles, and faithfulness, completeness, and minimality are not tested.
No main name-mover ablation or self-repair test on GPT-2 small IOI.
No IOI tests across other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks using the claimed components.
The paper compares extraction choices on synthetic Lean models, not methods applied to the GPT-2 IOI circuit.
No IOI evaluation of ablation, metric, prompt-distribution sensitivity, or the claimed circuit's explanatory coverage.
No IOI tests across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.
